traceability.evidence: Story file docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md exists and matches the content provided in the prompt (including acceptance criteria and detailed requirements).,Core rule implementations exist: - src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts implements the require-story-annotation rule. - src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts implements the require-req-annotation rule.,Both rules share the same function-detection scope and export semantics: - src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts defines DEFAULT_SCOPE = ["FunctionDeclaration", "FunctionExpression", "MethodDefinition", "TSMethodSignature", "TSDeclareFunction"]. - src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts also defines EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES = ["all", "exported", "non-exported"]. - src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts re-exports DEFAULT_SCOPE and EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES and defines shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority) that: - Returns false if node.type is not in scope. - Uses isExportedNode to implement exportPriority ("all" / "exported" / "non-exported"). - require-story-annotation.create() (src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts) reads options.scope and options.exportPriority, defaults to DEFAULT_SCOPE and "all", and passes a shouldProcessNode wrapper into buildVisitors(). - require-req-annotation.create() (src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts) imports DEFAULT_SCOPE and shouldProcessNode, applies the same scope/exportPriority logic, and gates all its node visitors via shouldCheck.,Arrow functions are explicitly excluded from required traceability by default, but can be present without being enforced: - DEFAULT_SCOPE does not include "ArrowFunctionExpression"; this is also the enum used in require-story-annotation.meta.schema, so scope cannot be configured to include arrows. - src/rules/helpers/require-story-visitors.ts defines a visitor for ArrowFunctionExpression, but every handler first calls options.shouldProcessNode(node); since "ArrowFunctionExpression" is not in DEFAULT_SCOPE, this returns false by default, so arrow functions are never required. - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts contains: - A valid case named "[REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED] unannotated arrow function allowed by default" with code const arrowFn = () => {}; (no @story), and this is in the valid array. - A valid case where an exported arrow function without @story is allowed when exportPriority is "exported".,JSDoc/comment parsing for annotations is implemented in shared helpers: - For @story: - src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts defines jsdocHasStory, commentsBeforeHasStory, leadingCommentsHasStory, linesBeforeHasStory, parentChainHasStory, fallbackTextBeforeHasStory, and combines them in hasStoryAnnotation(sourceCode, node). - hasStoryAnnotation is wrapped in try/catch and logs only when TRACEABILITY_DEBUG=1, satisfying error-handling requirements. - These helpers are injected into coreReportMissing/coreReportMethod in src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts. - For @req: - src/utils/annotation-checker.ts defines getJsdocComment, getLeadingComments, getCommentsBefore, combineComments and uses them in checkReqAnnotation(context, node, options). - checkReqAnnotation obtains jsdoc, leading, and before comments, combines them, and calls hasReqAnnotation(jsdoc, all, context, node) from ./reqAnnotationDetection (shared parsing strategy for requirement tags vs story tags). - If hasReq is false, it calls reportMissing which computes a user-friendly name and uses getNameNodeForReqReport to select an Identifier node where possible.,Requirement REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED is enforced for both rules: - require-story-annotation.meta.messages.missingStory provides an actionable error message: "Function '{{name}}' must have an explicit @story annotation... such as docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md." and auto-fix is enabled via fixable: "code". - src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts coreReportMissing and coreReportMethod construct ESLint reports with messageId: "missingStory", include data { name, functionName }, and provide both fix and suggest entries that insert an appropriate @story annotation. - require-req-annotation.meta.messages.missingReq says: "Function '{{functionName}}' is missing a required @req annotation. Add a JSDoc or line comment with @req (for example, '@req REQ-EXAMPLE')..." and uses data { name, functionName }. - annotation-checker.reportMissing builds the report for missingReq, including autofix when enabled via createMissingReqFix.,Configurable scope and exportPriority work identically for both rules: - require-story-annotation.meta.schema defines: - scope: array of strings with items.enum = DEFAULT_SCOPE and uniqueItems: true. - exportPriority: string enum = EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES. - additional options (annotationTemplate, methodAnnotationTemplate, autoFix) that do not affect which nodes are in scope. - require-req-annotation.meta.schema defines the same properties (scope, exportPriority) using DEFAULT_SCOPE and EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES, with additionalProperties: false. - require-req-annotation.create() normalizes options.scope and options.exportPriority to DEFAULT_SCOPE / "all" when omitted. - Both rules call shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority) from require-story-helpers to apply identical semantics, satisfying REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE and REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY.,Error location is normalized and anchored on function names where possible: - For @story: - src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts defines getReportedFunctionName(node) which uses extractName() to walk identifiers and keys, and getNameNodeForReport(node) which returns node.id or node.key when they are Identifiers, falling back to the node. - These are used by coreReportMissing/coreReportMethod to set node and data.{name, functionName} for context.report, satisfying REQ-ERROR-LOCATION. - For @req: - src/utils/annotation-checker.ts defines getReportedName(contextNode, parentNode) using getNodeName and defaults to "(anonymous)", and getNameNodeForReqReport(node) to prefer id/key Identifiers. - reportMissing(context, node, enableFix) uses these helpers and passes node: nameNode plus data { name, functionName: name } into context.report, also satisfying REQ-ERROR-LOCATION.,TypeScript-specific function constructs are supported and tested: - require-story-annotation: - src/rules/helpers/require-story-visitors.ts defines TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature visitors that call helperReportMissing with appropriate targets. - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts includes withTsLanguageOptions cases: - "[REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION] valid with annotation on TS declare function" (TSDeclareFunction). - "[REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION] valid with annotation on TS method signature" (TSMethodSignature). - Invalid cases asserting missing @story on TS declare function and TS method signature with expected fixes. - require-req-annotation: - src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts has explicit visitors for TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature that call runCheck(node) -> checkReqAnnotation. - tests/utils/annotation-checker.test.ts and tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts include TS-specific valid and invalid cases: - Valid TSDeclareFunction/TSMethodSignature with @req. - Invalid TSDeclareFunction/TSMethodSignature missing @req, asserting missingReq errors. - Tests run under TypeScript-aware parser options (tsRuleTesterLanguageOptions / withTsLanguageOptions), satisfying REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT.,User-facing rule documentation exists and aligns with the story requirements: - hasStoryAnnotation and related helpers are wrapped in try/catch and log only when TRACEABILITY_DEBUG=1, preventing crashes on malformed ASTs or missing APIs. - src/rules/helpers/require-story-io.* and require-story-helpers.* have multiple tests: - traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria and detailed requirements in docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md are implemented and verified by targeted rule code, shared helpers, comprehensive RuleTester suites, and aligned documentation. Both require-story-annotation and require-req-annotation enforce their respective annotations over the same function-like constructs (FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature) with consistent scope and exportPriority behavior, exclude arrow functions from required traceability by default, integrate TypeScript support, provide clear, actionable error messages anchored to function identifiers, handle malformed comments and edge cases gracefully, and are documented with examples and configuration options. All associated tests pass in the current Jest run, so this story is fully satisfied.
